newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr unmoved by budget, awaits RBNZ statement.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr unmoved by budget, awaits RBNZ statement.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar barely budged on Treasurer Winston Peters' first budget delivered on Thursday.
The currency closed just a few pips higher than its pre-budget level.

"The currency just hasn't moved," ANZ Bank's Head of Foreign Exchange Bill Murdoch said. "The foreign exchange market is probably looking more at tomorrow and the Reserve Bank statement in terms of the levels of the TWI and the 90-day bank bills."

The kiwi closed at US$0.0.6862/69, only a couple of basis points stronger than where it was trading before the budget was delivered. The Trade-Weighted Index finished at 67.29 against its opening level of 67.13.
ANZ's Murdoch said there was nothing in the budget likely to alter RB Governor Don Brash's view of the economy.
He said there were no major surprises in the budget.
Although there was a lower surplus forecast for 1997/98 and a higher bond tender programme, it would not cause financial markets any undue concern, he said.
Traders say the Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Statement at 9.00 a.m. (2100 GMT) would have a more direct bearing on the currency.
"The budget's impact on the currency was negligible," said one dealer, adding that there was nothing in it likely to change the RB's views in its MPS.
He said the smaller surplus of $1.5 billion and bigger bond tender programme could be a slight negative.
The market is factoring in the RB endorsing a 75-100 basis point easing in overall conditions on previous statement.
"I wouldn't have thought there was anything in the budget to cause the Reserve Bank to rewrite their statement for tomorrow," Murdoch said.
